messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @ryan (oncall) - alert: kv-cache per-rank entries >200M on prod-cluster-gpu-a, sustained for 7m. Continuous-batcher backlog increasing; some TP ranks unresponsive (NCCL retries). Auto-escalation triggered.

ryan (oncall): I'm awake. quick checklist: which model(s), pools affected, and are there 5xx customer reports?

sofia (eng-runtime): Observed on model:redwood/opt-xxl-q4a running on tensor-parallel 16. Rank 7 shows 3.8x entries vs median. NCCL ops are queuing and timing out; backlog correlates with KV write storms from prefix caching. No wide 5xx yet but elevated p95 and a couple errors in metrics.

dee (eng-ml): we took a weight quant and a small tokenizer change last deploy. Could quantization change token damping and increase persistent KV writes?

sofia (eng-runtime): Possibly. Also our partitioner has a corner-case: when token dims reduce below threshold, some empty buckets get rehashed to the same rank. That plus a sustained prefix-heavy workload -> one rank gets hammered.

kaye (support): Two paying customers in region eu-west reported timeouts and 502s in the last 8m. I opened tickets CS-2270 and CS-2272 and pinged their SREs. They asked for ETA.

ryan (oncall): Triage -> immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable kv_persistence for the impacted model to stop steady growth 2) lower continuous-batcher concurrency/turn off prefix batching 3) increase NCCL timeout to avoid hard stalls while we rebalance 4) route traffic off gpu-a pool if needed. Which do we have time for?

sofia (eng-runtime): I can toggle kv_persistence and batching via the control plane flag now. Increasing NCCL timeout requires a rolling restart of the runtime pods with env change (fast but careful). Routing traffic off pool will require a temporary scale up of pool-b fallback nodes. I'll start with flags.

sofia (eng-runtime): applying flag change:

```
# runtime hotpatch
MODEL_FLAGS="redwood/opt-xxl-q4a:kv_persistence=false,continuous_batching=false,max_batch_tokens=512"
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/hotpatch -d "$MODEL_FLAGS"
```

deploy-bot: Hotpatch accepted. Rolling flags to 8 runtime pods in gpu-a (concurrency=2).

sofia (eng-runtime): flags rolled to half the nodes. I've also queued an NCCL timeout bump via k8s patch to env NCCL_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 on a canary pair; will run restart when canary ready.

pagerduty-bot: Acknowledged by ryan (oncall).

kaye (support): Customers updated: "We are investigating and applying mitigations. Expect partial service recovery in ~20-30 minutes." They acknowledged.

sofia (eng-runtime): canary restart done. NCCL timeout increased; canary ranks handled rebalancing fine (no timeout). After full flag roll, per-rank memory on canary nodes dropped 68% and backlog decreased. However gpu-a still has 2 nodes with higher pressure.

dee (eng-ml): I prepared a partitioner patch that changes hash seed and ensures round-robin assignment for empty buckets. It also adds a guard for quantized-dim cases. Patch ready for runtime snakebite test.

sofia (eng-runtime): logs show this sequence in the hot interval (excerpt):

```
W kv_cache: rank=7 entries=198M median=52M skew=3.8
E nccl: retry_limit_exceeded op=allgather rank=7
I batching: inflight=120 backlog=410 avg_wait=5.4s
```

ryan (oncall): Given customer impact, do a controlled restart with partitioner patch on two of the affected nodes, then monitor. If stable, continue rolling restarts. Keep routing decisions conservative.

sofia (eng-runtime): executing controlled restart with partitioner patch on nodes gpu-a-02 and gpu-a-05. Command:

```
kubectl -n runtime set env ds/runtime NCCL_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 && kubectl rollout restart ds/runtime -l node=gpu-a-02,gpu-a-05
```

deploy-bot: Restart jobs started for nodes gpu-a-02,gpu-a-05.

sofia (eng-runtime): after restart and patch, rank distribution on patched nodes normalized. Rank-entry counts across cluster after two restarts: [54M, 50M, 48M, 51M, 53M, 49M, 56M, 52M, ...]. NCCL retries dropped to baseline.

kaye (support): Customer CS-2270 confirms traffic functional; they saw 30-40% slower responses for a short window but no further 502s. CS-2272 still seeing intermittent spikes; investigating with their SRE.

dee (eng-ml): I'm opening PR with unit test simulating quant reduced-dim hash collisions and ensuring even sharding. Also adding perf test that runs in CI to detect >2x per-rank skew.

sofia (eng-runtime): next steps: 1) finish rolling restart for remaining affected nodes with partitioner patch 2) revert kv_persistence toggle only after per-rank entry metrics stable for 1h 3) add telemetry alert for per-rank skew>2x and KV growth >10%/5m 4) bake canary into deploy pipeline to refuse deploys that produce skew in staging.

ryan (oncall): Handoff: @sofia you own post-mit monitoring and runtime PR. @dee own ML partitioner tests and PR. @kaye keep running customer comms and compile affected tenant list. I'll draft initial incident summary and timeline.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by assignment.

kaye (support): two customers affected total, time window ~18-51m depending on node. Offering credit and follow-up postmortem. Creating CS follow-ups.

sofia (eng-runtime): rolling restarts complete. cluster metrics stable. Removing hotpatch flags to restore normal batching for low-latency paths once we validate no re-growth in 1h.

ryan (oncall): closing the page, monitoring for 2h. Will publish postmortem skeleton in incidents folder and link to customers. Thanks team for quick coordination. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident closed by ryan (oncall).
